channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: RBA’s Hunter backs more hikes as inflation risks entrench
item.description: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter confirmed the need for further rate hikes this year, to keep inflation in check. This has increased the chances for a rate increase at the September 29 meeting.

item.title: Houthis push for control of Yemen highlands
item.description: Yemen’s Houthis pushed to seize strategic heights in Yemen on Monday to cut off the Red Sea coast from remaining areas held by Saudi-backed forces, after a report that US President Donald Trump had called off US strikes on the group at the last minute, Reuters reported.

item.title: ECB’s Lane says energy shock could delay inflation’s return to 2%
item.description: The European Central Bank (ECB) Chief Economist Philip Lane stated that the European economy will expand steadily at a moderate pace if the energy shocks ease, according to Le Temps.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds its nerve as Fed hawks meet RBA hike bets
item.description: The Aussie Dollar holds firm versus the Greenback at the start of the week, hovering near 0.7119 as risk appetite remains positive despite Fed officials turning more hawkish than expected, ahead of the Trump-Xi summit in the US, later this week.

item.title: Iranian President will head to New York for UN meeting
item.description: President Masoud Pezeshkian will lead an Iranian delegation at the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, amid renewed hopes for a diplomatic solution to the Middle East conflict, CNBC reported on Monday.

item.title: Gold declines to near $4,350 on rising odds of Fed rate hike
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) declines to near $4,365, snapping the two-day winning streak during the early Asian session on Tuesday. The precious metal loses ground on the prospect of further monetary tightening by the US Federal Reserve (Fed). Traders will keep an eye on the Fedspeak later on Tuesday.

item.title: The British Pound slips again as bets on an October Fed hike build
item.description: GBP/USD has stalled at 1.3400 in each of the last three sessions, and it trades just under that level again on Monday. The Dollar is up against most major currencies, so this is more a Dollar move than a Pound one.

item.title: The Japanese Yen keeps sliding after the Bank of Japan's split vote
item.description: Japan's markets are shut from Monday to Wednesday for national holidays, which is when a government that wants to move its currency gets the most for its money. USD/JPY is higher for a fifth session in six and is trading just below 157.50.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Bears lean on 0.5700 as RSI sinks
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar extends its losses for the second straight trading session, down 0.13% after last week’s Fed rate hike and a hawkish tilt within the board, which was reinforced by speeches of Fed officials on Monday. The NZD/USD trades at 0.5717.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: 100-day SMA caps bulls as range tightens
item.description: Silver price advance stalled at the 100-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) of $66.39 and is set to end Monday’s session with losses of 0.39% as the Greenback rises following last week’s Fed decision. The XAG/USD trades at $66.03 after reaching a high of $67.05.

item.title: Fed’s Collins eyes another hike as energy risks linger
item.description: On Monday, Boston Federal Reserve (Fed) President Susan Collins said the resumption of hostilities in the Middle East was a key reason for supporting the increase in the Fed funds rate last week.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Labour slack limits MAS tightening risk – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Jester Koh assesses Singapore’s soft labour market and its implications for Monetary Authority of Singapore policy. The Labour Market Pressure Index shows rising slack, which UOB links to weaker passthrough of supply-side shocks into inflation.

item.title: Gold price retraces as Fed hawks keep the US Dollar bid
item.description: Gold price retreats on Monday, down over 0.6% following last week’s Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike. That 25 bps hike initially pushed US bond yields higher, but the US Dollar Index (DXY) has recovered some ground on Monday despite Treasury yields falling in the back half.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Policy continuity offsets but cannot erase external headwinds – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong notes that Indonesia’s appointment of Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara signals fiscal continuity and discipline, helping to reduce domestic risk premia for the Rupiah.

item.title: Brent: Supply risks contrast softer prices – ING
item.description: ING strategists Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson note ICE Brent and WTI started the week lower despite persistent supply risks and elevated speculative length. They highlight Saudi Aramco’s curtailed allocations after pipeline damage, tighter European crude markets, and strong bullish positioning.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Inflation keeps MAS tightening risk alive - Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Henry Hao and Moses Lim highlight that Singapore’s August NODX growth was the strongest since 1998, driven by surging electronics and robust AI-related demand. They expect NODX to stay firm but moderate as base effects fade.

item.title: Fed's Musalem calls for more rate hikes
item.description: St. Louis Federal Reserve (Fed) President Alberto Musalem said interest rates likely need to rise further to tame inflation that is both demand- and supply-driven.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Upside bias intact despite mixed momentum
item.description: AUD/USD reverses its earlier gains on Monday as a broadly firmer US Dollar (USD) and hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations cap the upside.

item.title: South Korean Won: High-beta KRW needs foreign inflows – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong comments that USD/KRW eased as Korean equities rebounded and foreign investors briefly turned net buyers, but warns this may not mark a lasting shift.

item.title: Forex Today: Fedspeak takes centre stage alongside weekly ADP figures
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) has started the week on a positive footing, rapidly leaving behind two daily drops in a row and refocusing on the upper end of its recent range amid steady bets for extra rate hikes by the Fed and reignited geopolitical tensions.

item.title: BoC’s Macklem sees inflation drifting higher as uncertainty lingers
item.description: The Bank of Canada Governor, Tiff Macklem, said that he expects inflation to “drift up a little higher in the coming months,” and commented that “a new era of uncertainty is not going away any time soon,” as he spoke in Halifax.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average edges up as Trump floats a meeting with Iran
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades near 51,900 on Monday after its worst week since March. Crude Oil fell back under $100 after President Donald Trump told Fox News he'd probably be open to meeting Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian at the United Nations General Assembly this week.

item.title: British Pound loses grip as Fed hawks stay in charge
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) retreats by some 0.17% on Monday as the US Dollar (USD) trades in the green following last week’s Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike, which widened the interest rate differential between the US and the UK, while still-high energy prices put pressure on major central banks to ra

item.title: BoC’s Macklem: Rate decisions must look beyond initial Oil shock
item.description: Bank of Canada (BoC) Governor Tiff Macklem, speaking in Halifax, Nova Scotia, on Monday, offered a cautious assessment of the economy as higher energy prices and US tariffs create competing risks for inflation and growth.

item.title: WTI Oil extends losing streak as resilient Saudi exports outweigh Middle East risk premium
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil extends its decline for the fourth consecutive day on Monday, trading around $91.90 per barrel at the time of writing, down 3.54% on the day.

item.title: Gold struggles near $4,350 as hawksih Fed outlook supports the Greenback
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) remains on the defensive on Monday, pausing a two-day winning streak as expectations of additional Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hikes and a firmer US Dollar (USD) limit the upside.

item.title: Swiss Franc advances after recent sell-off, SNB in focus
item.description: USD/CHF extends its pullback on Monday after climbing to 0.8263 last week, its highest level since May 2025.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risk high as 160 seen possible against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that a reported Bank of Japan rate check briefly pushed USD/JPY below 157.0 and suggests authorities may focus on the pace of moves rather than a specific level.

item.title: Japanese Yen slides as Fed hawkishness, intervention fears grow
item.description: USD/JPY extends its advance on Monday and trades around 157.45 at the time of writing, up 0.36% on the day.

item.title: Euro struggles against US Dollar as hawkish Fed outlook weighs
item.description: EUR/USD trades with a downside bias on Monday as the US Dollar holds near recent highs, supported by expectations of additional Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hikes. Developments in the Middle East also remain in focus.
